deviations.what: the (B, L_kv) text padding mask is passed to mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention as a boolean mask reshaped to (B, 1, 1, L_kv), not converted to an additive mask
deviations.why: Equivalent semantics with no -inf arithmetic; diffusers' native backend passes the same boolean (B, 1, 1, L_kv) mask to torch SDPA. Verified with batch 2 and different padding per row.

deviations.what: RMSNorm computes in float32 with the float32 epsilon for every input dtype
deviations.why: torch.nn.RMSNorm(eps=None) does this (verified bit-exact for bf16). The spec assumed finfo(input dtype).eps, which for bf16 is 0.0078 and changed outputs by up to 90% in a test.

deviations.what: rotary and timestep frequencies are computed in float64 and rounded once to float32; long-position parity is judged against a float64 ground truth instead of torch CPU bits
deviations.why: torch CPU float32 exp is off by one ulp for 667 of the frequencies checked and torch CUDA differs again; at position ~2000 or t ~1000 one ulp of frequency is one ulp of the angle (~6e-5). The port's error vs float64 is no larger than the reference's (5.4e-5 vs 6.3e-5 for the timestep embedding). Recorded small-position calls match at <= 1.2e-7.

follow_ups: bf16 parity of attention and blocks is measured in spec 05 stage B against the float32 reference.
Spec 04 builds blocks on these primitives; dit_cases.replay_calls is reused there.

architecture_notes.note: At Baseline (50 220 video tokens, 28 heads of 64) mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention alone takes 1.57 s of a 2.24 s fused block (70%); at Smoke it is 6 ms of 44 ms. Estimated throughput about 11.5 TFLOPS in that kernel (scripts/profile_components.py (real Lite-distill weights, bf16, M3 Max, 2026-10-31)).
architecture_notes.optimization: Little to gain by rewriting SDPA itself; gains must come from fewer tokens or less attention work (spec 14), not from the glue.

architecture_notes.note: The rotation-matrix formulation kept for exact parity costs 24.5 MiB of float32 table at Baseline; building it takes 1.3 ms and applying it 15 ms per tensor (q and k: about 1.3% of a block).
architecture_notes.optimization: The video table is identical for every step and block: build once per generation. mx.fast.rope would save the table but changes rounding; only consider it with a bf16 parity check.

architecture_notes.note: LayerNorm in float32 plus apply_scale_shift and apply_gate_sum on (1, 50220, 1792) costs about 19 ms per use, about 7 uses per fused block (about 6% of a Baseline block).
architecture_notes.optimization: Fuse norm + scale/shift (+ gate) into one kernel (mx.compile or a custom Metal kernel); parity is easy to keep because each op is elementwise in float32.
